title: TARDIS — Time-Adjusted Roadmap Decision & Impact Score
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce TARDIS, a composite scoring framework that extends RICE-style prioritization by explicitly accounting for token-cost economics, latency-sensitivity of the use case, and time-to-value decay for long lead items. Goal: provide product and GTM teams a single sortable score that better predicts real production ROI when serving constraints (latency and token-cost) materially change the effective value of a feature.
background: Current RICE variants at Redwood capture Reach, Impact, Confidence, and Effort but fail to: (1) discount features whose value decays with time-to-ship (long lead features lose competitive advantage), (2) penalize high per-token cost features for hosted/Dedicated economics, and (3) reward features that reduce latency for latency-sensitive workloads. Several recent roadmap debates (see PM-5172 and PM-8427) highlighted cases where nominal RICE ranking favored features that later proved uneconomical when token/latency cost was included.
proposed_solution: Define TARDIS score: TARDIS = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort * TimeDecayFactor * EconFactor * LatencyFactor. Where TimeDecayFactor = 1 / (1 + TimeToValueWeeks/12). EconFactor = 1 / (1 + NormalizedTokenCostPerRequest). LatencyFactor = 1 + LatencyBenefitMultiplier * LatencySensitivity. Provide a shared spreadsheet and a lightweight UI widget in the Console Roadmap page that computes and explains the score per-initiative.
scoring_breakdown_example: Example: Feature A (high-reach chat routing): Reach=60k MAU, Impact=1.5 (revenue uplift proxy), Confidence=0.7, Effort=8pts, TimeToValue=6 weeks, TokenCostNormalized=0.12, LatencySensitivity=0.8, LatencyBenefitMultiplier=0.5. Base = (60 * 1.5 * 0.7)/8 = 3.9375. TimeDecayFactor=1/(1+6/12)=0.6667. EconFactor=1/(1+0.12)=0.8929. LatencyFactor=1+0.5*0.8=1.4. TARDIS=3.9375*0.6667*0.8929*1.4 ≈ 3.29. Compare against Feature B with lower token cost but slower time-to-value to see relative ranking shift.
decision_criteria_and_thresholds: Recommend buckets for triage: TARDIS > 4 => High priority candidate for next cycle; 2-4 => Consider in next two cycles; <2 => Backlog review. For cross-team initiatives include normalized token-cost thresholds: if per-request incremental cost > $0.05 and TARDIS improvement < 1.5, require engineering sign-off and cost-mitigation plan.
implementation_plan: 1) Publish canonical spreadsheet and sample scoring for 10 active initiatives (owner: Liam). 2) Run a 2-week calibration with PM and Eng for Cycle 41 to collect TimeToValue and TokenCost estimates. 3) Add a read-only TARDIS column to the Console Roadmap prototype (design: K. Morales). 4) Post calibration retrospective and adjust multipliers. Owner: Product Analytics + Platform Econ.
metrics_and_success_criteria: Primary: correlation of TARDIS rank vs. realized net margin impact after 3 months (target correlation > 0.55). Secondary: PM satisfaction survey > 80% find score helpful; reduction in post-launch cost surprises by 60% for features > P1.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: token-cost estimates are noisy. Mitigation: use 3-point estimates and require engineering verification for changes affecting Dedicated capacity. Risk: over-penalizing long-term platform bets. Mitigation: tag platform/strategic initiatives and allow override with mandatory justification and exec approval.

open_questions: Should TimeDecayFactor be linear in weeks or use a half-life style exponential decay?
How to attribute token-cost for mixed-model flows that use cached prefixes heavily?
When should product-strategic initiatives be allowed to opt out of TARDIS?
next_steps: 1) Platform Econ to provide normalized cost method by 2025-03-07. 2) Engineering to review gating rules and sign-off on cost attribution by 2025-03-10. 3) PMs to run TARDIS on all cycle candidates before roadmap sync on 2025-03-12.
notes: This framework is intentionally pragmatic: it should be lightweight enough to score dozens of candidates quickly while surfacing the two economics Redwood cares about most — per-token cost and latency — and balancing those against time-to-value and reach.
